binders: X: a real-valued random variable with distribution N(0,1) (standard normal) [PDF p.12/printed p.23 and PDF p.13/printed p.24, introduction to (2.12)].
lambda: an arbitrary real number, universally quantified by 'for all lambda in R' [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
hypotheses: X has the standard normal distribution N(0,1) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, sentence immediately before Equation (2.12)].
conclusions: For every real lambda, E[exp(lambda X)] = exp(lambda^2 / 2) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
definitions_and_conventions: The function lambda |-> E[exp(lambda X)] is called the moment generating function of X [PDF p.13/printed p.24, sentence immediately before Equation (2.12)].
N(0,1) denotes the standard normal distribution in the section's standing context [PDF p.12/printed p.23, paragraph introducing (2.10)].
E denotes expectation with respect to the probability law of X, and exp is the real exponential function, as used structurally in Equation (2.12) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
implicit_context: The underlying probability space is not named; only the law X ~ N(0,1) matters to the stated MGF identity [PDF p.12/printed p.23 through PDF p.13/printed p.24].
The formula asserts finiteness of E[exp(lambda X)] for every real lambda as part of the exact equality to the finite real number exp(lambda^2/2) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].

details: The equality holds for all lambda in R, with no restriction to a neighborhood of zero [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
X is the random variable and lambda is the deterministic real MGF parameter [PDF p.13/printed p.24, sentence and Equation (2.12)].
The identity is specific to X ~ N(0,1), not a claim about an arbitrary random variable [PDF p.13/printed p.24, sentence immediately before Equation (2.12)].
The relation is equality, not an upper or lower bound [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
The left side is E[exp(lambda X)]; the right side is exp(lambda^2/2) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
The factor 1/2 is inside the exponential exponent and applies to lambda squared [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
No exceptional real lambda values are excluded; lambda = 0 and negative lambda are included by the explicit all-real quantifier [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].

undebatable_constraints: The distributional hypothesis must be X ~ N(0,1), i.e. X is standard normal [PDF p.13/printed p.24, introduction to (2.12)].
The claim must quantify over every lambda in R [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
The integrand inside expectation must be exp(lambda X) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
The right-hand side must be exp(lambda^2/2) [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
The relation between the two sides must be exact equality [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].
There are no additional hypotheses or exceptional parameter cases in the source statement [PDF p.13/printed p.24, Equation (2.12)].

ambiguities.impact: A formal rendering may introduce routine probability-space and measurability structure, but it must not change the law-specific, all-real exact MGF identity; finiteness is already entailed by the displayed equality.

contract_plain_english: If X is a standard normal real random variable, then at every real parameter lambda its moment generating function exists and is exactly exp(lambda squared divided by two): E[exp(lambda X)] = exp(lambda^2/2).
